headline: ChatGPT's Chrome Extension Can Now Read Tabs and Act
dek: The updated extension lets the assistant compare open pages and complete tasks in the browser, at no extra cost.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: From one page to many tabs
body: OpenAI updated the ChatGPT extension for Chrome, giving the assistant access to open tabs and the ability to carry out tasks in the browser (Canaltech, Engadget).
Until now, it could only answer about the single page in view (Olhar Digital, Tecmundo).

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: Two modes: Chat and Work
s3.body: According to Canaltech, Tecmundo and Engadget, each mode has its own use.

points.t: Compares info across tabs, such as couches on different retailer pages (Canaltech, Engadget).
Fills out forms and adds events to calendars (Canaltech, Engadget).
Reviews open contracts and drafts an email with the best pick (Tecmundo).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Who can use it
body: According to Canaltech and Engadget, the update is open to every ChatGPT user, on any plan.
The extension also works on Edge, Brave and Opera, says Olhar Digital.

stat.cap: ChatGPT plan, according to Canaltech and Engadget

items.t: The system asks for authorization before acting on a new site (Olhar Digital).
Sensitive actions, like downloading files, ask for confirmation (Olhar Digital).
Task features also need the desktop app installed (Tecmundo).

caption.hook: OpenAI updated the ChatGPT extension for Chrome: the assistant can now read open tabs and carry out tasks.
body: According to Canaltech, Olhar Digital, Tecmundo and Engadget, the extension used to answer only about the single page in view. Now Chat mode compares information across tabs, and Work mode fills out forms and schedules events.

The update is open to every ChatGPT plan, per Canaltech and Engadget. Task features also need the desktop app installed. Olhar Digital reports the system asks for authorization on new sites and for confirmation on sensitive actions, such as downloading files.
